sections.evidence:
- D02 (Public Comment Period, L220) [c1]: "All applicants for solid waste permits that submit a new, renewal, closure or major amendment permit application are required to complete two public comment periods during the permitting process."
- D02 (Public Comment Period, L221) [c1]: "The applicant is required to publish each written notice once a week for two consecutive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation"
- D02 (Public Comment Period, L221) [c1]: "Each public comment period begins on the first day of the notice publication and continues until 30 days after the second publication."
- D03 (Public Notice and Participation in the CCR Permit Application Process, L198) [c1]: "If the modification would expand a facility or increase capacity, the process follows the same public participation procedures as outlined above for new solid waste permits."
- D03 (Public Notice and Participation in the CCR Permit Application Process, L195) [c1]: "The regulation requires that the public comment period last at least 45 days, with the public hearing scheduled at least 30 days following the public notice and the public comment period extending at least 15 days after the public hearing."
- D05 (Permit Modifications, L216) [c1]: "a permittee must request a major modification for the addition of, or a change in the design of, a liner and/or leachate collection system"
- D05 (Permit Modifications, L216) [c1]: "Major modifications require a public notice and public comment period under the same procedures as for issuance of initial permits."
- D05 (Permit Modifications, L217) [c1]: "lists certain categories of minor modifications that do not require a public notice or comment:"
- D05 (Permit Modifications, L218) [c1]: "addition of new groundwater monitoring wells or replacement of existing wells (of similar design and depth)"
- D05 (Public Comment Period, L240) [c1]: "a 35-day public comment period is provided for ADEM to receive comments related to the proposed permitting action."
- D05 (Public Comment Period, L240) [c1]: "The comment period will be extended to include comments submitted at a public hearing, if one is held on a proposed permitting action, if the hearing is scheduled after the end of the original 35-day comment period."
sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: one scenario total over three parallel State permit procedures, in which each of four permit actions follows a different stated rule (hook h25, sketch i01). Target medium (user 2026-10-10: "there is no slot for Easy Tier for this bundle, we should target medium and high. do your best."). Measured platform result pending. The structure follows the workspace's measured multi-cell total (aq-02564 q02 rev 1); the Wyoming and Virginia cells alone, asked as a difference, were quick-test too easy on the same bytes (aq-02626 q01), which is the stated risk.
- Dependency plan: Doc 2 L220 two comment periods for a new permit; L221 notices once a week for two consecutive weeks, each period from the first publication to 30 days after the second -> 7 + 30 = 37, twice = 74. Doc 3 L198 a capacity increase follows the new-permit procedures; L195 at least 45 days, hearing at least 30 days after notice, comment at least 15 days after the hearing -> hearing on day 40 gives 55. Doc 5 L216 liner design change = major modification, initial-permit procedures; L240 35 days, extended to include a hearing scheduled after they end -> hearing on day 40 gives 40. Doc 5 L217-L218 replacement wells of similar design and depth: no notice or comment -> 0. 74 + 55 + 40 + 0 = 169.
- Universe: four actions, all named in the question. Wyoming's new-permit process has exactly two comment periods (L218, L220); a Council hearing, if any, comes after the comment period (L224) and adds no comment days. Virginia's process has one comment period (L195-L197). Alabama's major modification has one (L216, L240); the well replacement has none (L217-L218).
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only source of Wyoming's two-period rule and "30 days after the second publication" (grep "second publication", "two public comment periods": D02 L220-L221 only). Doc 3 is the only source of the capacity-increase sentence and of "at least 15 days after the public hearing" (D03 L195, L198 only; Doc 4's 45s are Louisiana notice windows, discretionary extensions and settlement comment). Doc 5 is the only source of Alabama's modification classes and of the 35-day period with its hearing extension (grep "35-day", "similar design and depth": D05 only). Without any one document that State's figure is unknown and no total can be formed. The wording supplies the case (a week between notices, hearings on day 40, the four actions), not a rule or a classification.
- Selected-lever checks: Scatter the pieces: seven sentences in three documents, none of which states a total. Calculate across documents: 74 from Doc 2, 55 from Doc 3, 40 from Doc 5. Mentions it vs does it: the replacement well is a permit modification that draws no comment period (D05 L217-L218); giving it Alabama's 35 days yields 204, or 209 with the hearing-length period.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope / Misapplies a rule or premise): Virginia's "at least 15 days after the public hearing" (D03 L195) carried into Alabama, whose rule extends the period only "to include comments submitted at a public hearing" (D05 L240): 74 + 55 + 55 = 184. Mode 2 (Look-alike measure / Takes the wrong line item): Doc 2 prints "30-day public comment period" at L205 and L218 ("two, 30-day public comment periods"); 30 + 30 = 60 and 60 + 55 + 40 = 155. Recomputed 2026-10-10. Considered and not declared, to keep modes whose platform definitions fit and to stay within 50 words: Virginia left at its 45-day floor (159); the capacity increase read as an "other major modification" with 30 days (144); Alabama left at 35 days (164); the replacement well given a comment period (204); all three labels (140); one Wyoming period (132). The picks can be re-aligned with the wrong answers a difficulty run actually shows before Submit, without a new run.
- Calculation verification: python 2026-10-10 (caller): 7 + 30 = 37; 2 * 37 = 74; max(45, 40 + 15) = 55; max(35, 40) = 40; 74 + 55 + 40 + 0 = 169. Wrong routes 140, 144, 155, 159, 164, 184, 204, 209, 132. Day lengths are measured as the documents measure them, in days after a notice or hearing; counting both end days is not any of the three documents' convention (Doc 2 itself calls a period that runs "until 30 days after" a publication a "30-day" period).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 37, 74, 55 or 169 as a comment length, and none compares two States. The page overview lists none of the three rules (each "60-day public comment period" there is EPA's own comment window). Shortest route: Doc 2 L220-L221, Doc 3 L195 and L198, Doc 5 L216-L218 and L240, then four additions.
- Precision/readings: "at minimum" takes each State's floor (Virginia's "at least", Alabama's extension only as far as the hearing; Wyoming's length is fixed by its notices). "notices a week apart" fixes the gap that "once a week for two consecutive weeks" leaves open. A hearing 40 days after notice meets Virginia's 30-day lead (L195) and Alabama's 35 days' notice (D05 L232). "capacity increase" is the document's "increase capacity"; "liner redesign" is "a change in the design of, a liner"; "identical replacement monitoring well" falls within "replacement of existing wells (of similar design and depth)". If the well replacement were processed inside the liner modification, Alabama's total is still 40. Whole days, no rounding. Louisiana and Wisconsin are not in the scenario: Louisiana's pre-application notice also takes comments with no stated length (D04 L218), and Wisconsin's periods conflict (D06 L217 vs L228).
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (intake: incomplete false, gap 0 for all six documents).
- Style/set review: 58 words (the form warns above 60), one ask, paraphrased ("coal-ash", "public-comment days", "liner redesign"). The scenario figure 40 is printed in all three ticked documents ("40 CFR"). Only question on this bundle so far; sketch i02 (EPA's own hearing dates against Virginia's post-hearing rule) shares the 15-day sentence of Doc 3, so at most one of q01/i02 is submitted.
- Warnings answered: see the floor result recorded after the preflight below.

sections.question: A utility needs a new coal-ash landfill permit in Wyoming (notices a week apart), a capacity increase at a Virginia landfill and, at an Alabama landfill, a liner redesign and an identical replacement monitoring well. Hearings on the capacity increase and the redesign come 40 days after notice. At minimum, how many public-comment days is that in total?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, Public Comment Period): an applicant for a new solid waste permit, which covers a coal-ash landfill, must "complete two public comment periods during the permitting process", one on the complete application and one on the proposed permit.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 2, Public Comment Period): the applicant publishes each notice "once a week for two consecutive weeks", and "Each public comment period begins on the first day of the notice publication and continues until 30 days after the second publication."
Step 3. Calculation (Doc 2): with the second notice one week after the first, days from the first notice to the close of one Wyoming comment period: 7 + 30 = 37.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 3, Public Notice and Participation in the CCR Permit Application Process): a permit modification that "would expand a facility or increase capacity" follows "the same public participation procedures as outlined above for new solid waste permits". Those require "that the public comment period last at least 45 days, with the public hearing scheduled at least 30 days following the public notice and the public comment period extending at least 15 days after the public hearing."
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 3): with the hearing 40 days after the notice, the earliest close of Virginia's comment period, in days after the notice: 40 + 15 = 55. That is later than the minimum length quoted in Step 4, so the hearing rule sets Virginia's minimum.
Step 6. Source input (Doc 5, Permit Modifications): a change in the design of a liner needs a major modification, and "Major modifications require a public notice and public comment period under the same procedures as for issuance of initial permits." Replacing existing groundwater monitoring wells with wells "of similar design and depth" is listed among the minor modifications "that do not require a public notice or comment", so the replacement well adds no comment days.
Step 7. Source input (Doc 5, Public Comment Period): "a 35-day public comment period is provided", and it "will be extended to include comments submitted at a public hearing, if one is held on a proposed permitting action, if the hearing is scheduled after the end of the original 35-day comment period." A hearing 40 days after the notice falls after that period ends, so the liner redesign's comment period runs to the hearing, 40 days after the notice.
Step 8. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 3): Wyoming's total over its two comment periods, in days: 37 + 37 = 74.
Step 9. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 3): Wyoming and Virginia together, in days: 74 + 55 = 129.
Step 10. Final answer (Doc 2, Doc 3 and Doc 5): adding Alabama's liner redesign, in days: 129 + 40 = 169.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 3's 15 days after a hearing is Virginia's rule; Doc 5 extends Alabama's 35 days only to the hearing. Carrying it over gives 184. Look-alike measure: Doc 2 labels Wyoming's periods "30-day", but each runs 37 days; the label gives 155. Gold: 169.
